robot: Franka Panda on an Omron mobile base with a torso lift (RoboCasa PandaOmron); the arm takes absolute joint position targets

frame.suite: the RoboCasa kitchen's world frame (metres, z up)
frame.base_text: the mobile base's starting placement: on the floor at the base's origin, +X the way the arm faces, +Y the robot's left, +Z up; it stays where the base started (driving the base does not move this frame)

arm.note: Panda arm: 7 absolute joint position targets (rad); the gripper is open or closed only. There is no end-effector command.

notes: The arm takes absolute joint position targets only (no end-effector command): describe_robot gives the joint limits. The base and the torso lift are driven with execute_trajectory space native, action_type joint_position (13 numbers, one row per 0.05 s control step): arm_joint1..7 (keep the current targets, cmd_* in proprio_now), grip (+1 closes, -1 opens), base_x, base_y, base_yaw (the mobile base's velocities in its own frame, normalised to [-1, 1]), torso (the lift's velocity, normalised), hybrid_mode (-1, the default). proprio_now has eef_right_x/y/z (the grip site's position in the world frame), the joints (robot0_joint1..7, mobilebase0_joint_mobile_forward/side/yaw, mobilebase0_joint_torso_height) and cmd_* (the last command). The poses the tools report are in the base's starting placement. The cameras ride on the robot; each frame comes with its current calibration.
